items.stem: Why is making application servers stateless important for horizontal scaling?

options.text: Any request can be served by any instance, so you can add instances behind a load balancer freely
options.rationale: Correct: statelessness removes server affinity that blocks scale-out.

options.text: It eliminates the need for a database
options.rationale: State moves to shared stores, not disappears.
Statelessness is unrelated to consistency guarantees.

items.explanation: Correct: statelessness removes server affinity that blocks scale-out.

items.stem: What risk does a poorly chosen shard key introduce?

options.text: Hotspots, where one shard receives disproportionate load
options.rationale: Correct: skewed keys concentrate traffic on a single shard.

options.text: Elimination of the need for caching

items.explanation: Correct: skewed keys concentrate traffic on a single shard.

items.stem: Which statements about caching are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A read-through cache can reduce load on the primary datastore for hot keys
options.rationale: Correct: frequently read data is served from cache.

options.text: Cache invalidation strategy must be designed to avoid serving stale data
options.rationale: Correct: invalidation is a core, hard part of caching.

options.text: Caching removes the need to ever read the database
options.rationale: False; cache misses and writes still hit the datastore.

options.text: A CDN is only useful for dynamic, per-user API responses
options.rationale: False; CDNs excel at static/cacheable content.

items.explanation: Correct: frequently read data is served from cache.; Correct: invalidation is a core, hard part of caching.
